newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury trading volume swells post-FOMC--GovPX.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury trading volume swells post-FOMC--GovPX.

text.p: Volume in U.S. Treasury securities jumped sharply along the short end of the yield curve following the Federal Reserve's announcement on Tuesday that short-term interest rates will be raised a quarter of a percentage point, according to GovPX Inc.
"It looks like the activity was clearly in the one-year Treasury bill. For some reason, volume just took off," said Ted Hersey, vice president of new products at GovPX Inc.
Similarly, the five-year note turned in heavy volume as well, he said.
In the half hour from 1400 EST/1900 GMT to 1430 EST/1900 GMT, volume totaled a staggering $11.1 billion in trades, Hersey said, adding that such a figure was "extremely high for a half hour."

Before the Fed's announcement, the Treasury yield curve flattened slightly, with the spread on two-year notes to 30-year bonds marking just under 68 basis points. However, that spread flattened to about 65.6 basis points, coinciding with the Fed's announcement, he said.
"It's interesting because the spread had widened just in the hour or so before there," he said.

Tuesday's volume -- just over $96 billion -- surpassed the $93.5-billion level achieved at 1500 EST/2000 GMT on January 31, 1996, the last time the central bank moved on rates. At that time, the fed cut the federal funds rate by 25 basis points. The last time the central bank raised rates was over two years ago.
